answer: In an AI-agent market trading saffron, voting power is proportional to escrowed collateral, not account count, and collateral stays locked for 30 days after each vote. Splitting $1,000 among a thousand fake agents gives no more influence than staking it through one. This denies attackers an oasis of free voting power: even when identity costs hit their nadir, buying more influence still requires tying up more capital.
